title: Borrowed Code, Real Consequences: What OPTIMJACK Teaches Us
description: The OPTIMJACK supply chain attack involved exploitation of a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into customer accounts. This malicious code was served from the vendor's legitimate CDN and affected at least 178 organizations, including major media, technology, and financial services brands. The injected script performed cryptocurrency wallet address swapping, payment card skimming, and attempted delivery of mobile exploit kits. Optimizely patched the vulnerability and removed the malicious code within a day. The incident highlights the risks posed by third-party scripts with dynamic execution privileges and underscores the importance of strict segmentation to isolate sensitive user inputs from potentially compromised vendor scripts.
